Evidence: Police reports, court documents, victim injuries
#Aletheia #Australia #Justice 🌐

News reporting frames the police action as a straightforward law-and-enforcement response to community safety concerns and unlawful violence.

Police have now arrested and charged six teenagers in relation to the bashing of a 13-year-old boy in Ellenbrook last weekend that was filmed and shared online.

They are accused of being among a group of youths who savagely attacked the boy at Coolamon Oval between 5.30am and 6.30am on Sunday morning.

The attack, which left the young boy at the centre of it with a concussion, black eye, and bruising to his body, was filmed by “a number of offenders” and uploaded to social media, Perth Children’s Court heard on Friday.

Police had begun investigating the attack when they were first made aware of the video, which had been widely disseminated online earlier this week.

It made for confronting viewing, with the group hurling abuse at the young boy as he was attacked on the ground and made to take his clothes off.

On Friday a 14-year-old boy appeared in court after he was charged with one count of with intent to harm, did an act causing bodily harm, and one count of aggravated armed robbery.

On Saturday, a WA Police spokesperson said they had arrested five more youths - a 13-year-old girl, two 14-year-old girls, a 16-year-old girl and a 17-year-old boy - who were then charged with the same offences.

None of them can be named for legal reasons. They are due to appear in Perth Children’s Court on Saturday.

On Friday, the court heard the 13-year-old alleged victim was punched without warning as he tried to walk away from the group, before they set upon him in an assault that lasted between five to 10 minutes.

Two youths in the group were carrying knives, the court was told.

The court heard the fight had followed a previous altercation involving the 13-year-old and of the youths in the group at the park.

The 14-year-old boy charged over the attack allegedly kicked the victim “square in the face” before kicking and stomping on him with other co-offenders while the boy lay on the ground.
